title: B1 Grammar Quiz 1 — Present Perfect Continuous, Passive Voice, Second Conditional

questions.question: I ___ for you for an hour!
questions.explanation: Present Perfect Continuous = have/has been + -ing. Emphasises duration of an ongoing activity.

questions.question: She looks tired. She ___ all day.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect Continuous explains a visible result of a recent ongoing activity.

questions.question: I ___ three cups of coffee today. (completed action, number given)
questions.explanation: When the number of completed actions is stated → Present Perfect Simple: 'have drunk three cups'.

questions.question: How long ___ English?
questions.explanation: 'How long' + ongoing activity → PPC: 'have you been learning'. The learning is still happening.

questions.question: This bridge ___ every year.
questions.explanation: Passive Present Simple = is/are + past participle. 'The bridge is cleaned (by someone)'.

questions.question: The letter ___ last Monday.
questions.explanation: Passive Past Simple = was/were + past participle: 'was sent'.

questions.question: The new school ___ next year.
questions.explanation: Passive Future: 'will be + past participle': 'will be built'.

questions.question: The windows ___ by the cleaners every week.
questions.explanation: 'Windows' is plural → 'are cleaned'. Passive Present Simple plural.

questions.question: The Mona Lisa ___ Leonardo da Vinci.
questions.explanation: Passive + agent: 'was painted by + the agent'.

questions.question: If I ___ a million dollars, I ___ travel the world.
questions.explanation: Second Conditional (unreal present/future): If + Past Simple, would + base verb.

questions.question: If she ___ taller, she could be a model.
questions.explanation: In Second Conditional, 'were' is preferred for all subjects (especially in formal English): 'If she were'.

questions.question: What ___ you do if you ___ the boss?
questions.explanation: Second Conditional: 'What would you do if you were...?' — both parts must match.

questions.question: She knows five languages. She ___ be very clever.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong logical deduction from evidence: we are almost certain.

questions.question: He ___ be at home — his car isn't here.
questions.explanation: 'Can't' expresses negative deduction — we are almost certain something is NOT true.

questions.question: I'm not sure where she is. She ___ be at the gym.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses possibility when we are not certain: 'maybe she is'.

questions.question: When I arrived, the film ___ already ___.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect = had + past participle. Shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.question: She failed the exam because she ___ enough.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect shows the earlier action: 'hadn't studied' (before failing).

questions.question: By the time we got there, they ___.
questions.explanation: 'By the time' + Past Simple triggers Past Perfect for the earlier action: 'had left'.

questions.question: 'I love chocolate.' → She said she ___ chocolate.
questions.explanation: Present Simple → Past Simple in reported speech: 'loves' → 'loved'.

questions.question: 'I will help you.' → He promised he ___ help me.
questions.explanation: 'Will' → 'would' in reported speech.

questions.question: 'Where do you live?' → She asked me where I ___.
questions.explanation: Reported Wh-questions: question word + subject + verb (no inversion). Tense shifts back: 'live' → 'lived'.

questions.question: The book ___ I told you about is excellent.
questions.explanation: Defining relative clause for a thing → 'which' (or 'that'). 'What' cannot be used as a relative pronoun here.

questions.question: My brother, ___ is a doctor, lives in Paris.
questions.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses (with commas) about people → 'who'. 'That' cannot be used in non-defining clauses.

questions.question: I hate this job. I wish I ___ a better one.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + Past Simple' expresses a present wish about something we want to be different.

questions.question: She can't drive. She wishes she ___ drive.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + could' expresses a wish about ability in the present.

questions.question: ___ is good for your health.
questions.explanation: Gerunds (-ing form) can function as subjects of a sentence: 'Swimming is good'.

questions.question: She is interested ___ learning Italian.
questions.explanation: 'Interested in' is a fixed expression. After prepositions, always use -ing form.

questions.question: ___ being tired, she finished the project.
questions.explanation: 'Despite/In spite of' + noun/gerund. 'Although/Even though' + clause (need subject + verb).

questions.question: He studied hard. ___, he passed the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Therefore' = as a result, for that reason. Shows logical consequence.

questions.question: The project ___ yet.
questions.explanation: Passive Present Perfect: 'have/has + been + past participle': 'hasn't been completed'.
